brewing.notes: A common starting point for herbal infusions: boiling water, about five minutes.

description:
An infusion of the leaves and buds of wild ese trees, a variable-leaf crabapple, growing at 3000 to 3500 metres around Luhuo on the Tibetan plateau's southeastern edge.

Brew it as you would other herbal infusions. If the plant is new to you, check that it is safe for you first, especially when pregnant or on medication.
history: In Tibetan areas ese leaf drink was long kept for chieftains, lamas, nobles, honoured guests and festivals, and it appears in Tibetan medical writing. The modern product was developed by researchers hired by the county in 2005. It received geographical indication protection on 30 September 2010, covering seven townships of Luhuo.
processing: Dried plant material, as with most herbal infusions.
harvest_season: The first flush of the year's new buds.
taste_profile: Clean, fragrant and sweet, with a long finish and a soft mouthfeel; holds up to repeated steeping.
vintage_note: Herbal infusions are not sold by vintage: buy recent stock and use it within a year or so.
